children: Megaport's bull at Macquarie recommends investors drop any resistance to the compute-as-a-service provider's strong momentum. One of the investment bank's analysts tells clients in a note that the Australian company's reallocation of pooled processors to a new contracts highlights management's focus on returns. They explain that the customer's A$282 million prepayment gives Megaport a capex payback period of about eight months, compared with between 16 and 22 months for pooled capacity. This reduces utilization and funding risk, the analyst adds. Macquarie keeps an outperform rating on the stock and raises its target price 8.4% to 34.70 Australian dollars. Shares are down 0.5% at A$20.525. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
